item.research_question: How do multiple metal-nitrogen bonds affect the activity and durability of high-entropy alloy electrocatalysts?
item.material_system: N-doped high-entropy alloy (HEA) electrocatalyst with a Pt-rich shell and a N-doped PtCoFeNiCu core on a carbon support (denoted as N–Pt/HEA/C)
item.processing_route: thermal annealing process and an acid-etching de-alloying strategy
item.test_conditions: rotating disk electrode (RDE) testing in 0.1 M HClO4 aqueous solution, membrane electrode assembly (MEA) testing in HDV applications
key_findings: The N–Pt/HEA/C catalyst showed a high mass activity of 1.34 A mgPt–1 at 0.9 V for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR)
The N–Pt/HEA/C catalyst demonstrated excellent stability in both RDE and MEA testing
The formation of multiple metal–nitrogen bonds improved the corrosion resistance of the 3d transition metals and enhanced the ORR durability
The N–Pt/HEA/C catalyst exhibited a more positive half-wave potential (E1/2) of 924 mV than Pt/HEA/C and commercial Pt/C
The N–Pt/HEA/C catalyst showed a high current density of 1437 mA cm–2 at 0.7 V and only 18 mV drop at 0.8 A cm–2 after 30,000 voltage cycles
item.mechanism: The enhanced ORR activity of N–Pt/HEA/C originated from the optimized adsorption energy of intermediates, resulting in the tailored electronic structure formed upon N-doping
quotes: Multiple Metal–Nitrogen Bonds Synergistically Boosting the Activity and Durability of High-Entropy Alloy Electrocatalysts

records.text: Paper card. Question: How do multiple metal-nitrogen bonds affect the activity and durability of high-entropy alloy electrocatalysts?. System: N-doped high-entropy alloy (HEA) electrocatalyst with a Pt-rich shell and a N-doped PtCoFeNiCu core on a carbon support (denoted as N–Pt/HEA/C). Processing: thermal annealing process and an acid-etching de-alloying strategy. Test conditions: rotating disk electrode (RDE) testing in 0.1 M HClO4 aqueous solution, membrane electrode assembly (MEA) testing in HDV applications. Findings: The N–Pt/HEA/C catalyst showed a high mass activity of 1.34 A mgPt–1 at 0.9 V for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR); The N–Pt/HEA/C catalyst demonstrated excellent stability in both RDE and MEA testing; The formation of multiple metal–nitrogen bonds improved the corrosion resistance of the 3d transition metals and enhanced the ORR durability; The N–Pt/HEA/C catalyst exhibited a more positive half-wave potential (E1/2) of 924 mV than Pt/HEA/C and commercial Pt/C; The N–Pt/HEA/C catalyst showed a high current density of 1437 mA cm–2 at 0.7 V and only 18 mV drop at 0.8 A cm–2 after 30,000 voltage cycles. Mechanism: The enhanced ORR activity of N–Pt/HEA/C originated from the optimized adsorption energy of intermediates, resulting in the tailored electronic structure formed upon N-doping. Quote: "Multiple Metal–Nitrogen Bonds Synergistically Boosting the Activity and Durability of High-Entropy Alloy Electrocatalysts"
